scope_summary: Formation counters and names (and events, places, objective labels) during long Play on the audited build (f10fe585...), the carried item of docs/STAGE8_SPEC.md sections 22.3, 23.2 and 23.4. 21 runs on the deterministic motion driver (tools/visual/motion.js, the WebGL draw skipped; vis-lib.js codes every map-layer item every frame and computes in each frame the layout a fresh view would give): the three benchmark Play runs replicated (exactly MOTION.VIS), Landscape with counters at 1600x900 over 08:30-11:30 and 12:00-15:00 at 1/2x, the whole day at 4x, at 60 fps, Follow off, Watch, both headquarters' readings, a selection, one hour at three pacings; the Landscape and the paper map over 09:00-12:00 and the day; the phone (390x844) with counters and in its default Landscape. Two real-time runs on a visitor's page with Play and Pause by real clicks (with and without the WebGL draw), each compared with the driver at matched pacing and at 30 fps. Stills drawn with WebGL while Play runs. Detail: README.md, tables.md/json, items.json, runs/.

findings.title: Landscape with counters: during Play the same five to eight formations' counters are hidden most of the time, up to 28 s (100 clock minutes) at a stretch; the benchmark's 4,033 ms is only its window
findings.subsystem: map layer in motion (app.js mlCollect priorities; the MLS stabiliser, implementation PR 8C)
findings.user_impact: A visitor following the morning at 1/2x in Landscape with counters (52 s of playback) sees the four divisions of Murat's Cavalry Reserve, both Guard cavalries and Miloradovich unlabelled most of the time; Miloradovich's counter vanishes at 09:15 and stays hidden for 28 s of playback. The figures and outlines remain, unidentified; each counter is reachable by hover or keyboard (decision 39).
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/visibility/tables.md (hybrid-0830, hybrid-1200, hybrid-4x-day, hybrid-0830-60, hybrid-fixed-0830, hybrid-watch-0830, hybrid-fr-0900, hybrid-al-0900); items.json; runs/raw-hybrid-*.json; stills/hybrid-0830-f450.jpg
findings.expected: Each formation in view labelled most of the time during Play with short, bounded gaps, as the default Landscape achieves (83-89% drawn, gaps <=2.5 s).
findings.observed: Formation-frames drawn 64-77% (a fresh layout in the same frames 73-89%). Over 08:30-11:30 at 1/2x, Follow on: d'Hautpoul 9.8%, Russian Guard cavalry 15.8%, Walther 16.2%, French Guard cavalry 16.5%, Miloradovich 17.5%, Kellermann 36.6%, Nansouty 46.5%; longest gaps Miloradovich 27,667 ms (99.8 clock min from 09:15), Russian Guard cavalry 17,667 ms, Walther 15,333 ms, French Guard cavalry 13,233 ms, d'Hautpoul 12,667 ms, Kellermann 12,333 ms. 12:00-15:00: d'Hautpoul 15,300 ms (60 min). Follow off: d'Hautpoul 6.9%, 21,967 ms. 60 fps: 67.1%, the same 27,667 ms gap.
findings.repro: node tools/audit-post8/visibility/long-play.js --runs hybrid-0830 (tools/visual/motion.js VIEWS.hybrid: 1600x900, Study, Landscape with counters, the Field vantage; seek 08:30, Follow on, 1/2x, eight frames at rest, Play to 11:30, 30 frames at rest); node tools/audit-post8/visibility/analyse.js
findings.cause_hypothesis: Crowding on the French left (the Santon, Murat's divisions, the Imperial Headquarters, Lannes) and on the Stare Vinohrady heights, decided by a priority rule that ranks divisions by strength (cavalry last), plus the stabiliser's hold strategy for the whole of Play (Play is a motion source even with a still camera): an item not drawn needs room at two successive 333 ms passes, held places are kept.
findings.cause_verified: partly: a fresh layout in the same frames starves d'Hautpoul (3.8%), the Russian and French Guard cavalries (10.4%, 20.8%) and Walther (26.1%) nearly as much (crowding + priority, inherited), while Miloradovich (fresh 47.9%) and Kellermann (42.1%) lose mainly to the stabiliser; 26-56% of the hidden formation-frames had room in that very frame.
findings.remedy: Treat it with V-2's priority change, then let a held item that a fresh layout would place ahead of a kept lower-priority item take its room at a pass (section 22.3's 'kept first while moving' variant met the ceilings but failed seven runs' visibility baselines); re-measure the 16 motions and the long runs; an owner decision on decision 240 (a)'s order and the MOTION.VIS baselines.
findings.risk: room given to one formation is taken from another (a selection shows it: Saint-Hilaire 80.6% to 51.1% when Nansouty is selected)
findings.validation: the long runs here re-run: no formation under 50% over 08:30-11:30; gaps bounded in clock minutes; the 16 motions within their ceilings

findings.title: The formations a live event names are hidden while their event's label is drawn (the Guard cavalry clash 0-16%; Miloradovich at the face-about 0-40%)
findings.user_impact: The visitor reads 'Rapp's counter-charge breaks the Chevalier Guard' or 'Kutuzov orders the 4th Column to face about' on the map while the counters of the formations it names are absent; a counter that vanishes as its event begins reads as the formation leaving.
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/visibility/README.md table C; tables.json runs.*.evForms (with freshLayoutShare); stills/
findings.expected: While an event is live, the formations it names labelled, as the event label itself is (decision 39 protects the label).
findings.observed: Landscape with counters, share of the named formations' in-view frames drawn while the event's label is drawn: guard-broken (11:15-13:15) French Guard cavalry 0.0% / 10.8% / 4.2% (08:30, 12:00 and 4x-day runs), Russian Guard cavalry 1.5% / 16.0% / 4.2%; guard-attack Russian Guard cavalry 3.7-12.2%, Russian Guard infantry 8.3-34.6%; face-about Miloradovich 0.0-40.0%; blasowitz Russian Guard infantry 0.0-24.0%; hq-forward Imperial Headquarters 77.7%. All named formations: 53.8-66.2% (Landscape 75.2-80.2%, paper map 96.7%, phone with counters 40.2%). The event labels themselves 100%.
findings.repro: as V-1; analyse.js's evForms over runs/raw-hybrid-0830.json, raw-hybrid-1200.json, raw-hybrid-4x-day.json
findings.cause_hypothesis: mlCollect gives a counter pri 3 + rank (echelon, strength) with no term for live events; live events' labels are protected and placed first, on the ground where their formations fight.
findings.cause_verified: yes for the rule (app.js:5126, 5144, 5476); for the Guard cavalries a fresh layout also fails (0-16%), so no stabiliser change alone would show them; for Miloradovich, the Imperial Headquarters, Rivaud and Caffarelli the fresh layout would draw them (33-100%) and the stabiliser hides them.
findings.remedy: Raise every formation a live event names (and its collected parent) to the selected family's priority (pri 1) or protect it while the event is live; measure on the 16 motions and the long runs (an owner decision if MOTION.VIS moves).
findings.dependencies: owner decision if MOTION.VIS baselines move
findings.risk: more protected items crowd others out near the action
findings.validation: each named formation drawn >=80% of its event's frames in the long runs

findings.title: No check can see long gaps: the motion benchmark's longest-hidden measure saturates at its own 121-frame window, and the one check that plays the whole day counts drops, not how long a formation stays hidden
findings.user_impact: None directly; a regression that hides formations for longer stays invisible to the safeguard decision 257 (b) relies on.
refs: app.js:10045-10048 (the self-test's day at 1/2x: one mlLayout every ten clock minutes, dropped items <= 19)
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/visibility/runs/sum-bench-hybrid.json (Nansouty, Walther, Miloradovich hidden in 121 of 121 frames); README.md table D
findings.expected: A visibility safeguard able to see the gaps a visitor meets in normal playback.
findings.observed: 28 formations x 121 frames = the baseline's 3,388; 121 x 33.3 ms = 4,033 ms, the most the measure can report. The long runs' gaps are 12-28 s; in the hybrid runs a formation is hidden for a whole 90-frame window in 6/14 to 17/17 windows. The benchmark's one Play run per presentation starts from a seek at 09:00. The self-test's 4D pacing check plays the whole day at 1/2x but samples one layout pass every ten clock minutes and counts the items dropped (at most 19), in its own state: it cannot see a formation hidden for an hour.
findings.repro: node tools/audit-post8/visibility/long-play.js --runs bench-hybrid; compare thresholds.js MOTION.VIS['hybrid-play']
findings.cause_hypothesis: the motion block was designed for short motions (60-90 frames) and its Play run inherits that length; the day-long check predates the stabiliser and counts drops per sample
findings.remedy: Add a long Play run (08:30-11:30 at 1/2x on the driver without the draw, about 1-3 minutes) to the motion block, judged per formation on the share drawn and the longest gap in clock minutes.
findings.dependencies: owner decision on the new limits
findings.validation: the new run fails on this build until V-1/V-2 are addressed, or its limits are set at this build's values by the owner

carried_status.item: counters hidden during playback (4,033 ms; dropped at rest)
carried_status.status: confirmed, open, and understated by the benchmark
carried_status.evidence: The 4,033 ms is the benchmark's whole 121-frame window (Nansouty, Walther, Miloradovich hidden in 121 of 121 frames). Over 08:30-11:30 Walther's and Miloradovich's counters and four more (d'Hautpoul, both Guard cavalries, Kellermann) are hidden 12-28 s at a stretch (Miloradovich 27,667 ms, 09:15-10:55); Nansouty's gaps are shorter (2.3-3.7 s) but he is drawn in only 36-61% of his frames in view; real time with the draw reproduces the driver frame for frame. Dropped at rest: Nansouty, Walther and Miloradovich are dropped by crowding at 09:14 in that view (a fresh view drops them too); the kept places add 0-3 formations per run (V-5). Findings V-1, V-2, V-3.

strengths: The instrument reproduces the benchmark exactly, and the app's own loop in real time (with the WebGL draw, real clicks) equals the driver frame for frame at matched pacing: the motion driver is a faithful instrument
Protected items were never hidden: 0 frames in 21 runs (live events in every run, the selection and its family in the selection run; no hover was exercised); every live event label drawn 100%
The default Landscape and the paper map keep every formation labelled most of the time over long playback (83-93%) with gaps of at most 2.5 s and no formation systematically starved
The army headquarters' counters stay drawn 83-98% with gaps of at most 0.7 s at 1600x900
The 30 fps benchmark pacing is representative of a 60 Hz display (67.1% against 67.6% over three hours, the same longest gap)
